options: Use object lookup map instead of nested if
explanation: Object map replaces conditionals: const discounts = {premium: 0.2, standard: 0.1}; more maintainable.

options: No refactoring needed; code is clear
Use reduce to eliminate loop and accumulator
Use forEach instead of for loop
Extract price calculation to separate function
explanation: reduce eliminates manual loop and accumulator: items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.quantity, 0)

options: Use switch statement for multiple checks
Combine all conditions in single if
explanation: Early return inverts conditions: if (!user.name || !user.email || user.age <= 0) return; else console.log('valid')
Compose validations: const isValid = compose([validateEmail, validateAge, validateName]); cleaner flow.

options: Enables parallel requests instead of sequential
explanation: Promise.all runs requests in parallel instead of sequentially, improving performance.

options: Extract URL construction into helper function
Create generic fetch wrapper for API calls
Use template literals for string building
explanation: Create apiFetch wrapper: const apiFetch = (endpoint) => fetch(`${API_URL}${endpoint}`).then(r => r.json())

options: Re-throw error after logging for caller handling
Use finally block to ensure cleanup
explanation: Catch and re-throw lets caller handle error: catch (e) { console.log('error: ' + e); throw e; }

options: Use template literals instead of concatenation
Refactor to async/await to reduce nesting
explanation: async/await eliminates callback hell: const user = await getUser(id); const post = await getPost(user.id)

options: Extract validation logic into reusable validator factory
Use regex for all pattern matching
explanation: Create validator factory: const createValidator = (field, rules) => (value) => rules.forEach(r => r(value, field))
